name: Lutronic Genesis

lead: Genesis-style treatment uses a long-pulse 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser at low energy to warm the skin without damaging the surface. Lutronic, a South Korean device maker, offers the Xerf platform used for this kind of toning.
Clinics offer it for redness, uneven tone, texture and pores. A course usually involves several sessions spaced weeks apart, and clients typically resume activity the same day.

paras: Providers say 1064 nm energy penetrates beyond the epidermis, and repeated pulses accumulate heat in the dermis that stimulates fibroblasts, collagen and microcirculation [2]. The surface stays intact.

Clinics describe mild redness lasting hours for toning, and temporary redness, bruising or spot darkening for vascular or pigment settings [1]. One manufacturer page lists superficial pigment such as freckles as better treated with other wavelengths [2]. It is delivered by a clinician.

angle.text: A series of quick, no-downtime laser sessions aims at a more even, smoother and less red complexion. Clients typically return to normal activity the same day.

lead: Lutronic Genesis refers to a non-ablative Nd:YAG laser skin-toning treatment of the "laser genesis" type, delivered on long-pulse 1064 nm platforms such as Lutronic's Xerf [1][2]. People get it to even out skin tone, reduce diffuse redness and refine texture, with no real downtime.

Providers describe the technique as gentle repeated pulses that build heat in the dermis and stimulate collagen and circulation over a series of sessions [1][2]. Clinic descriptions say sessions run roughly 20 to 45 minutes, are spaced several weeks apart, and leave mild redness that fades within hours [1].

The material on this treatment comes mainly from clinics and device makers, and no peer-reviewed trials specific to Lutronic's protocol were located. Naming varies, since "Genesis" is also used by other manufacturers for the same style of treatment.

paras: Lutronic's Xerf is described by a clinic as a long-pulsed 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser used for vascular lesions, pigment, hair reduction and rejuvenation, with a toning application sometimes called laser genesis [1]. Another source describes a Genesis mode as a quasi-long pulse of about 0.3 ms delivered at repeated rates [2].

Providers say 1064 nm light is absorbed by hemoglobin and melanin, and long pulses heat gradually, causing collagen remodeling over time [1]. Accumulated heat is said to stimulate fibroblasts and microcirculation while leaving the epidermal barrier intact [2].
No studies found for Lutronic's Genesis protocol specifically. Descriptions of the technique come from clinic and device-maker pages [1][2].
People use it as a low-risk maintenance treatment for complexion quality, particularly diffuse redness and texture, often as a course rather than a single visit [1].
